$comment: Single source of truth for geometry parameter definitions. Read by lib/geometry/parameters.ts and backend/geometry/parameters.py. Lengths are metres, angles are degrees, ratios are dimensionless. Body heights are measured from the body floor plane, so ride height moves the whole body relative to the ground. A parameter with a "default" was added after the first release: geometries stored before it existed are completed with that value.

parameters.label: Wheelbase
parameters.tooltip: Distance between axle centres. Sets body length together with the overhangs; a longer body has more wetted area but a gentler rear pressure recovery.

parameters.label: Front overhang
parameters.tooltip: Nose to front axle. Longer overhangs allow a more gradual front-end shape and move the front wheels further behind the stagnation region.

parameters.label: Rear overhang
parameters.tooltip: Rear axle to tail. Gives room for rear taper, deck and diffuser, which control the size of the wake.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.tooltip: Overall body width. Drag force scales with frontal area, which grows almost linearly with width.

parameters.label: Roof height
parameters.tooltip: Roof crown above the body floor. Overall height = ride height + roof height. Raises frontal area and the size of the rear separation region.

parameters.label: Body (beltline) height
parameters.tooltip: Height of the shoulder line above the floor, where the greenhouse starts to narrow. A higher belt makes the full-width lower body taller.

parameters.label: Hood length
parameters.tooltip: Nose to windshield base. Positions the cabin along the body and therefore the length left for the roof and the rear slope.

parameters.label: Hood (cowl) height
parameters.tooltip: Height of the hood at the windshield base, above the floor. Together with nose height it sets the hood slope and how hard the flow is turned upward.

parameters.label: Front bumper (nose) height
parameters.tooltip: Height of the nose's upper edge above the floor. A tall, blunt nose increases the stagnation area and forebody drag.

parameters.label: Rear bumper (tail) height
parameters.tooltip: Height of the tail's upper edge (deck trailing edge) above the floor. A higher tail reduces the effective rear slope but enlarges the base.

parameters.label: Windshield angle
parameters.tooltip: Windshield inclination from horizontal. Steeper (more upright) screens turn the flow harder and raise forebody drag.

parameters.label: Rear window angle
parameters.tooltip: Rear window (backlight) inclination from horizontal. Near 30 deg strong trailing vortices form and drag peaks; steeper slopes separate fully like a squareback.

parameters.label: Rear deck length
parameters.tooltip: Length of the trunk lid behind the rear window. A deck lowers the effective rear slope and lets separated flow re-attach.

parameters.label: Front plan taper
parameters.tooltip: Fractional narrowing of the body toward the nose in plan view. Taper eases the flow around the front corners.

parameters.label: Rear plan taper (boat-tail)
parameters.tooltip: Fractional narrowing of the body toward the tail in plan view. Boat-tailing shrinks the base area and raises base pressure.

parameters.label: Cabin width ratio
parameters.tooltip: Roof width as a fraction of body width (tumblehome). A narrower greenhouse reduces frontal area and the width of the upper wake.

parameters.label: Ride height
parameters.tooltip: Height of the body floor above the ground. Lower ride height restricts underbody flow, which changes underbody suction and exposes less tyre.

parameters.label: Ground clearance limit
parameters.tooltip: Configured minimum allowed clearance. The actual lowest point (floor, skirts, splitter) is computed from the geometry and a warning is raised if it falls below this limit.

parameters.label: Floor flatness
parameters.tooltip: 0 = exposed, rough underbody; 1 = fully panelled flat floor. Smooth floors reduce underbody drag and let the floor and diffuser generate suction.

parameters.label: Diffuser angle
parameters.tooltip: Upsweep angle of the rear floor. Moderate angles recover pressure and add downforce; beyond roughly 10-14 deg the diffuser flow tends to separate.

parameters.label: Diffuser length
parameters.tooltip: Length of the upswept floor section ahead of the tail. Sets the diffuser area ratio together with angle and ride height.

parameters.label: Front splitter extension
parameters.tooltip: Length of the flat plate protruding ahead of the nose at floor level. High pressure above it and fast flow below produce front downforce.

parameters.label: Rear spoiler angle
parameters.tooltip: Inclination of the lip spoiler from horizontal. A steeper blade stands higher in the flow, raising deck pressure (less lift) at a drag cost.

parameters.label: Rear spoiler height (blade)
parameters.tooltip: Blade length of the lip spoiler at the tail edge; its vertical rise is blade length x sin(angle). Zero removes the spoiler.

parameters.label: Spoiler width
parameters.tooltip: Span of the lip spoiler (limited to the tail width). A wider spoiler acts on more of the deck.

parameters.label: Rear wing chord
parameters.tooltip: Chord of a separate rear wing mounted above the deck. Zero removes the wing.

parameters.label: Rear wing angle
parameters.tooltip: Wing angle of attack (trailing edge up is positive). Downforce rises roughly linearly until the wing stalls; induced drag rises with the square of its lift.

parameters.label: Side skirt depth
parameters.tooltip: How far the sill skirts extend below the floor. Skirts limit air leaking in from the sides, which helps the underbody hold low pressure.

parameters.label: Wheel diameter
parameters.tooltip: Overall tyre diameter. Larger wheels need larger arch openings and also change the gearing (road speed per engine revolution).

parameters.label: Tire width
parameters.tooltip: Tyre section width. Wider tyres present more frontal area to the flow below the body.

parameters.label: Wheel exposure
parameters.tooltip: 0 = wheels shrouded with flush covers; 1 = open arches with the tyre standing proud of the body. Exposed rotating wheels are a major drag source.

parameters.label: Door mirror width
parameters.tooltip: Lateral span of each door mirror housing; 0 removes the mirrors (camera pods are a few centimetres wide). Mirrors add frontal area and a wake of their own, typically 3 to 5 % of a car's drag.

parameters.label: Rim openness
parameters.tooltip: 0 = closed aero covers; 1 = thin, widely spaced spokes. Open rims pump air through the rotating wheel and add ventilation drag in the wheelhouse.

parameters.label: Cooling intake area
parameters.tooltip: Open grille and intake area as a share of the frontal area. Air that passes through the radiator loses momentum, which is cooling drag. 0 = sealed front or closed shutters; electric cars need about a third of what a combustion car does.
